title: AI News Radar
description: Real-time panoramic intelligence radar for global frontier AI breakthroughs.

items.title: Databento, which offers market data APIs and says it has contracts with five of the six largest frontier AI labs, raised a $100M Series C at a $1.1B valuation (FinTech Global)
items.content_text: Financial data provider Databento secured $100 million in Series C funding led by Fifth Down Capital, reaching a $1.1 billion valuation. The firm provides real-time and historical market data via a unified API and has successfully secured enterprise contracts with five of the six largest frontier AI labs.

items.title: Jensen Huang's resignation is a setback for US open models, as his funding gave open-source developers time to find their footing and will very likely dry up (Nathan Lambert/Interconnects AI)
items.content_text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned, creating uncertainty around his strategic funding for the open-source model ecosystem. Huang previously used significant capital to support open-source models as a hedge against large customers developing internal silicon, a strategy now facing potential abandonment as Nvidia prioritizes stabilizing operations and hardware delivery.

items.title: Sean Duffy blames Friday's FAA outage on copper-to-fiber wiring work at a remote facility, saying contractor L3Harris may have installed a "faulty router" (Joseph Pisani/Wall Street Journal)
items.content_text: FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford and officials identified that the nationwide flight ground stop was caused by maintenance work upgrading copper wiring to fiber at a remote facility. The investigation currently focuses on whether long-time contractor L3Harris installed a faulty router or committed installation errors, which triggered a network flood within the air traffic control system.

items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon takes the MathArena crown but costs 15 times more than GPT-6.1 Sol
items.content_text: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon model surpassed OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol to top the MathArena math benchmark, with Claude Fable 5.2 ranking second. Despite its superior performance, the model incurs reasoning costs 15 and 40 times higher than GPT-6.1 Sol, respectively, while exhibiting significant issues with excessive compute time usage.

items.title: Anthropic says outdated prompting habits are slowing down Claude Opus 5.5
items.content_text: Anthropic announced that users should abandon legacy prompting habits for the Claude Opus 5.5 model, as it now features native adaptive reasoning. The company advises setting the effort level to 'medium' and utilizing single-prompt comprehensive inputs to enhance task execution efficiency and optimize cost-to-performance ratios.

items.title: Trump Media faces a Nov. 30 deadline to repay up to $1B in convertible bonds sold last May to fund a "bitcoin treasury," as its shares are down 60+% this year (Financial Times)
items.content_text: Trump Media & Technology Group (NASDAQ: DJT) faces a critical liquidity event as creditors may demand the repayment of up to $1 billion in convertible notes by November 30. On-chain data indicates the transfer of 4,259 BTC in collateral to Crypto.com, highlighting acute financial stress amidst a year-to-date share price decline of over 60% and $1.8 billion in cumulative losses.

items.title: Tesla posts its Cybercab Autonomy Subscription Agreement, requiring personal buyers to pay a mandatory $299/month on top of the vehicle's $29,990 purchase price (Fred Lambert/Electrek)
items.content_text: Tesla released the Cybercab Autonomy Subscription Agreement, requiring a $299/month software fee on top of the $29,990 purchase price. The contract prohibits personal owners from adding the vehicle to the Robotaxi fleet and grants Tesla unilateral authority to modify geofenced operational zones and pricing, effectively reclassifying owners as variable-rate lessees.

items.title: Italy's data protection agency fines Meta €805M for allegedly accessing Android users' photos and videos without their consent or informing them (Reuters)
items.content_text: Italy's privacy regulator has imposed a 805 million euros penalty on Meta Platforms Ireland after finding that the company accessed photos, videos, and related information stored on Android devices without obtaining specific user permission. The case focuses on a Facebook feature that offered users photo and video suggestions from their phone galleries while they were browsing the app. According to the authority, the feature allowed access to gallery content without providing users with clear i

items.title: The OpenAI board member who fired Sam Altman says we still can’t trust AI CEOs
items.content_text: Helen Toner, Executive Director of the Center for Security and Emerging Technology at Georgetown University and a former OpenAI board member, stated that accountability mechanisms in AI frontier labs are structurally flawed when confronted with commercial incentives. She argues that relying on individual leadership integrity and voluntary safety accords is insufficient to guarantee safety in large-scale model development.

items.title: Beware the New AI-Fueled Ransomware Boom
items.content_text: Cynthia Kaiser, former FBI cyber deputy director, and Allan Liska, threat intelligence analyst at Recorded Future, report a 20-40% spike in ransomware incidents this summer, totaling nearly 3,000 cases. AI is being integrated into attack chains to enhance phishing efficacy and negotiation, with groups like Gentlemen, Qilin, and Akira leveraging LLMs to optimize operations.

items.title: How the Swiss city of Lugano is trying to reinvent itself as a crypto hub to boost its economy by launching its own token LVGA, partnering with Tether, and more (Financial Times)
items.content_text: The city of Lugano, Switzerland, has launched a crypto-hub initiative by issuing the LVGA token for public services and forming a strategic joint venture with stablecoin issuer Tether. This policy aims to attract blockchain firms and stimulate the local economy through digitized financial infrastructure.

items.title: OpenAI reassigns robotics researchers to other teams as general-purpose models might make specialized robotics AI unnecessary
items.content_text: OpenAI is dissolving its dedicated robotics division, reassigning researchers to the main research team under Chief Research Officer Mark Chen and the Applied organization led by Greg Brockman. The shift reflects a strategic pivot towards using general-purpose models like GPT-6 Astra, which have outperformed specialized robotics models in spatial reasoning and task execution, for embodied AI development.

items.title: Anthropic can already retrain Mythos with "a fraction of the compute originally needed," says former researcher Coxon
items.content_text: Former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon revealed that the compute trajectory disclosed in the company's IPO roadshow indicates a significant jump in training efficiency for its Mythos model. He argues that algorithmic improvements are scaling super-exponentially, noting that Mythos can now be retrained with a fraction of its original compute requirement, with such gains trending toward automation.

items.title: Runway's open-source Praxis-1 turns video AI into a robot controller
items.content_text: AI company Runway has released its robot model Praxis-1 with open weights and source code. The model uses what it learned from video to control robots and shows promising results in the company's own tests. Runway has released Praxis-1, its AI model for controlling robots. The company first introduced Praxis-1 in late September but initially gave access only to select partners. Alongside the release, Runway published a detailed research report with new performance tests. Runway's model weights

items.title: Microsoft says all Microsoft 365 products are operational, ending an outage that disrupted governments, traders, hospitals, and businesses around the world (Bloomberg)
items.content_text: Microsoft experienced a significant global cloud infrastructure failure around November 13, disrupting critical services including Microsoft 365, Outlook, Teams, and SharePoint Online. The company implemented emergency recovery measures such as traffic throttling, route redirection, and extending email timeout thresholds to 48 hours, eventually stabilizing systems while ruling out malicious activity.

items.title: Sources: despite Nvidia's 20+ years of business in China, Jensen Huang struggled to gain access to policymakers driving Beijing's chip self-sufficiency campaign (Eleanor Olcott/Financial Times)
items.content_text: Nvidia’s board is investigating CEO Jensen Huang’s dealings with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang to assess potential foreign intelligence penetration of company trade secrets. Amid tightening US semiconductor export controls, this investigation forces a critical re-examination of Nvidia’s China market strategy and the compliance risks of executive interactions with geopolitically sensitive entities.

items.title: Operand, which offers AI-powered due diligence tools for PE firms, raised $31M across a seed and a Series A led by Khosla Ventures at a $220M valuation (Lucinda Shen/Axios)
items.content_text: Operand, which uses AI to do due diligence for private equity firms, raised $31 million in seed and Series A funding, CEO Ram Gorthi tells Axios Pro exclusively.

items.title: WhiteMatter, which builds "guardian" AI agents to oversee file access, software use, decision making, and actions of existing AI agents, raised a $20M Series A (Alice Tecotzky/Business Insider)
items.content_text: WhiteMatter raised $20 million in Series A funding, led by Blumberg Capital. The company utilizes a 'Guardian Agent' architecture that assigns a real-time monitoring node to every enterprise AI agent, auditing file access, software calls, and decision logic to prevent unauthorized or rogue actions during autonomous execution.

items.title: Charta Health, which offers AI-powered tools to automate medical chart review, billing, and coding workflows, raised a $55M Series B led by Insight Partners (Jessica Hagen/MobiHealthNews)
items.content_text: The round is the company's third in less than two years and brings its total funding to $85 million. — Global Investing

items.title: Luminal, which provides an inference cloud and develops inference compiler software to test running AI models on different chips, raised a $25M Series A (Chris Metinko/Axios)
items.content_text: Luminal, a search compiler and inference cloud provider, raised a $25 million Series A led by Standard Capital, CEO Joe Fioti tells Axios Pro exclusively.

items.title: Cambridge, UK-based Tendrils, which is designing a CPU architecture with thousands of cores operating in parallel, raised $30M led by Benchmark (John Reynolds/Tech.eu)
items.content_text: Cambridge-based Tendrils Compute has raised $30 million in a round led by Benchmark. The company is developing a novel high-performance CPU architecture featuring thousands of parallel cores, aiming to deliver superior compute density and energy efficiency for intensive AI workloads compared to traditional general-purpose processors.

items.title: JD.com completes its takeover of German electronics retailer Ceconomy, after acquiring a ~60% stake for ~$1.5B, following the EU's approval of the deal (Tomoko Wakasugi/Nikkei Asia)
items.content_text: JD.com has completed its acquisition of roughly 60% of German consumer electronics retailer Ceconomy for €1.34 billion ($1.47 billion). Approved by the European Commission under fair market conditions, the deal combines JD's Chinese e-commerce expertise with Ceconomy's network of over 1,000 European stores, including MediaMarkt and Saturn.

items.title: Analysis: Sam Bankman-Fried's $500M Anthropic investment in 2021 would be worth ~$37B if Anthropic lists at ~$1.5T; he relinquished his stake in 2024 for ~$1.3B (George Hammond/Financial Times)
items.content_text: Jailed cryptocurrency mogul loses out on windfall from early investment in the AI lab — Sam Bankman-Fried will miss …

items.title: Free speech group FIRE says DOJ and DHS will end efforts to curb "ICE Sightings - Chicagoland" Facebook group and Eyes Up iOS app, which report on ICE activity (Kanishka Singh/Reuters)
items.content_text: The U.S. government has agreed to end efforts pressuring Facebook and Apple to restrict platforms reporting on ICE immigration enforcement activity following a First Amendment settlement with free speech group FIRE.

items.title: US officials say Trump is not expected to raise allegations of a Chinese intelligence operation involving Jensen Huang during his upcoming meeting with Xi (Dan Mangan/CNBC)
items.content_text: Senior U.S. officials stated that President Donald Trump is not expected to raise allegations involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his alleged ties to a cloud-computing company suspected of bypassing chip export controls during his upcoming China visit. The trip will focus on trade agreement implementation, with Elon Musk joining the delegation.

items.title: Tesla says "select customers" can now place orders for its Cybercab "for personal use", for $30K plus a required $299/month Autonomy Subscription to operate (Kara Carlson/Bloomberg)
items.content_text: Tesla has opened Cybercab orders to select customers in Texas and Florida for $29,990. While the vehicle features no steering wheel or pedals, owners are required to subscribe to a $299/month 'Autonomy Subscription' and are restricted to operating within Tesla-defined Robotaxi service geofences.

items.title: AI's impact on math is a preview of what AI will do to AI research, with AI matching top human researchers potentially just a couple of years away (Dwarkesh Patel/Dwarkesh Podcast)
items.content_text: Recent internal data from Anthropic and OpenAI indicates an exponential rise in AI's role in R&D, with AI participation in Anthropic’s research tasks jumping from under 1% to 26% within a year. Experts project that the automation of AI research could lead to AI matching human expert capabilities across all fields within the next few years.

items.title: Doc: Amazon, wary of AI agents favoring sites with better data, plans to gather data on nearly every product sold anywhere, including by crawling rivals' sites (Greg Bensinger/Reuters)
items.content_text: Amazon is developing the 'World Product Graph' project, which plans to crawl competitor websites to index virtually every product sold online. The strategy aims to feed massive data into the Alexa AI shopping assistant, improving response accuracy and ensuring that consumers remain within the Amazon ecosystem even during research phases.

items.title: Sources and messages: Jensen Huang misled several Nvidia leaders, including general counsel Tim Teter, about the nature of his relationship with Alice Huang (Reuters)
items.content_text: Newly disclosed information reveals that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang provided misleading statements to company leadership, including general counsel Tim Teter, regarding his relationship with Alice Huang. This incident is directly linked to ongoing compliance investigations into Megaspeed's alleged illicit acquisition of restricted Nvidia chips.

items.title: Sources: the FAA outage occurred after an update to the private communications network that connects the ATC system caused the system to reboot and crash (Kierra Frazier/CBS News)
items.content_text: U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy stated that the nationwide FAA ground stop was caused by a system crash triggered by an update to the aging air traffic control communications network. Security patches led to data overload on routers, causing system reboots. The network is operated by third-party contractor L3Harris.
